samples.text:
The bar chart shows the percentage of adults in one country who did six different sports and exercise activities in 2008 and in 2023.

In 2008 swimming was the most popular activity with 21% of adults. Gym was second with 14%, and then cycling was 11%, football 10% and running 9%. Yoga was the less popular, only 3% of people did it.

In 2023 the situation was changed. Gym become the most popular activity with 24%, and swimming decreased to 13%. The biggest change was in gym, which rose by 10 percentage points. Running also increased a lot, from 9% to 17%, so it almost doubled. Yoga went up to 11%, which is a big increase. Cycling was nearly same, it was 11% and 12%. However, football fell from 10% to 7%.

Overall, the gym, running and yoga became more popular between 2008 and 2023, but swimming and football was less popular than before. Cycling did not change much in this period.
samples.why: Figures accurate and all activities covered · overview present but basic and placed last · list-like, mechanical presentation · limited vocabulary · several verb-form and article errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The chart compares the proportion of adults in a particular country who participated in six sports and fitness activities at least once a month in 2008 and 2023.

Overall, the gym overtook swimming as the most popular activity over the 15-year period. Participation in gym workouts, running and yoga rose considerably, whereas swimming and football became less popular and cycling remained almost unchanged.

In 2008, swimming was clearly the leading activity, attracting 21% of adults, followed by the gym at 14%. By 2023, however, their positions had been reversed: the figure for gym use climbed to 24%, while swimming dropped by 8 percentage points to 13%. Running showed a similarly impressive rise, almost doubling from 9% to 17%, and yoga, which had been the least popular activity in 2008 with only 3%, grew to 11%.

Football was the only other activity to see a decline, with participation falling from 10% to 7%. Cycling, meanwhile, was remarkably stable, being the choice of 11% of adult in the first year and 12% in the second.
samples.why: Clear overview identifying the main shift · key features well highlighted and grouped · good range of cohesive devices · some less common collocations · frequent error-free sentences with one minor slip.

samples.text:
The bar chart shows what percentage of adults in one country engaged in six forms of sport and exercise at least monthly, comparing 2008 with 2023.

The period saw a clear shift in preferences: gym-based exercise replaced swimming at the top of the ranking, and running and yoga also gained substantially in popularity. Swimming and football, on the other hand, lost ground, while cycling held steady.

Swimming was the most widely practised activity in 2008, with 21% of adults taking part, but by 2023 this had fallen to 13%. Over the same period, gym participation rose from 14% to 24%, making it comfortably the most common activity by the end of the period.

Among the remaining activities, the growth in running was particularly striking, with the proportion of participants nearly doubling from 9% to 17%. Yoga saw the sharpest relative increase of all, more than tripling from a mere 3% to 11%. By contrast, football declined modestly from 10% to 7%, and cycling was virtually unchanged, edging up by a single percentage point to 12%.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected with a well-placed overview · accurate, selective figures for comparison · cohesion managed effortlessly · wide, precise vocabulary · varied structures, error-free.
